findings.summary: The header logo link's accessible name is Homepage, which replaces the visible wordmark WaterLevels.org on every public page.
findings.fix: Remove aria-label="Homepage" from the brand link. Keep the droplet SVG inside the aria-hidden mark, and let the visible WaterLevels.org text be the accessible name.
findings.evidence: with WaterLevels.org and the SVG in span.mark[aria-hidden].

findings.summary: Flood alerts and state pages expose two banner landmarks because the site header and the page hero are both header elements, and neither banner has a label.
findings.fix: Change the hero from header.state-hero to a div, or move that hero inside main. Leave Navigation::BarComponent as the only header so the page has one banner.
findings.evidence: <header class="site-header"> in the nav component plus <header class="state-hero"> before main on alerts and state directory pages.

findings.summary: The map page has no h1, and its only headings are inside hidden panels, so heading navigation finds no headings on load.
findings.fix: Add one h1 as the first heading in main, for example Water level map. Keep Data layers and Search stations as h2 elements, and place the h1 outside any hidden panel.
findings.evidence: No h1. First headings are h2 Data layers (line 71, aside hidden) and h2 Search stations (line 206, .map-mobile-search hidden).

findings.summary: The map is one image whose name omits stations and flood status; role=img hides markers, popups, and attribution, and the station list stays in a hidden panel.
findings.fix: Remove role=img from the Leaflet container. Give each marker role=img and an aria-label of the station name and status (the title option is only a tooltip). Keep the stations-in-view list available on load, outside the hidden settings panel, point the map at it with aria-describedby, and list every station in view rather than stopping at 40.
findings.evidence: setAttribute role=img; aria-label Water gauges map. Use Search stations or the Stations in view list. aside#map-settings-panel is hidden. Markers use title and keyboard:false. The Search stations control is in .header-actions, hidden from the md breakpoint up.

findings.summary: Station cards on the flood alerts and state directory pages wrap each station h3 inside the card link.
findings.fix: Put the anchor inside the heading, for example h3 then a with the station name. Do not wrap the h3 in the card link. County and state h2 elements that contain their own links can stay as they are.
findings.evidence: link_to path, class: station-card do ... h3 name, so the heading is a child of the anchor.

passed: html lang is en (3.1.1), and no in-scope passage is in another language (3.1.2)
Each of the 12 pages sets a unique descriptive title as page name | WaterLevels.org (2.4.2)
The skip link is first, targets #main on every page, and is shown on focus (2.4.1)
Each page has one main; primary, mobile, and footer navs have distinct names
Home, alerts, state, about, FAQ, contact, subscriptions, privacy, terms, disclosures, and AUP each have one h1 and do not skip heading levels
FAQ questions put the button inside the h3, and geolocation dialogs use an h2
No img, picture, video, or audio in the in-scope templates; no content image is missing alt
Decorative SVGs are aria-hidden, and icon-only buttons and links have accessible names
Map legend swatches are aria-hidden and paired with text labels
notes: On about, FAQ, disclosures, flood alerts, and state pages the h1 is before #main, so the skip link moves past the page heading. 2.4.1 is still met because the repeated header is bypassed. Files: pages/about.html.erb:15, pages/faq.html.erb:21, pages/disclosures.html.erb:16, alerts/show.html.erb:21, states/show.html.erb:28.
main#main has no tabindex=-1. Current HTML moves the sequential focus start to the fragment, so this was not filed as a failure.
Decorative inline SVGs omit focusable=false. They are removed with aria-hidden, often on a parent, and are not tab stops in current browsers.

Privacy repeats Your Rights and Controlling Your Personal Information as an h2 (privacy.html.erb:162) and an h3 (line 272). Both describe their sections, so this was not filed under 2.4.6; distinct wording would separate them in the heading list.
The map page has no footer or contentinfo landmark. Attribution links are rendered inside the map widget.
Cloudflare Turnstile on the contact form and the subscription page is third-party markup; its images and headings are not in these templates.
ul role=list restores list semantics after Tailwind preflight sets list-style: none. It was not treated as a redundant landmark.

Titles were confirmed from public_meta_tags (site WaterLevels.org, reverse) and the meta-tags gem, not from a rendered browser. Gauge detail, admin, and mailers were out of scope. No raster images were available to compare with alt text.
